model_rule: Shell commands verify correctness, not LLM judgment

findings.gap: Output verification for most file types (.md, .jsonl, .txt, .js, .ts, and more) only checks existsSync(). Content validation is applied exclusively to .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .html, .htm, and .json. A task that writes an empty or malformed .md file passes output checks.
findings.evidence: find-gaps.ts:388: existsSync(absOutputPath) — existence-only check; lines 428-476: only six file extensions get content validation (png/jpg/html/json). All other extensions skip validation entirely and pass through the if/else chain without any format or content check.
findings.correction: Extend ValidationRuleSets to cover .md (non-empty + frontmatter parse) and .jsonl (one valid JSON object per line). Allow check definitions to specify arbitrary content validation rules (jq schema, grep pattern, line count range) so playbook authors can define contract-complete checks.
findings.test_to_write: tests/output-content-validation.test.ts — test that a task producing an empty .md file fails a content-aware check, and a task producing valid .md content passes.

findings.gap: The type: 'ai' check delegates to an LLM for subjective verification. The mental model states checks should be deterministic shell commands. An AI check is non-deterministic and requires a configured AI provider — it is the definition of 'vibes' over verified correctness.
findings.evidence: ai-check.ts:179-186: runAiCheck() calls createAIFactory() which uses an LLM to evaluate a natural-language assertion. The SYSTEM_PREAMBLE (line 97) explicitly instructs the LLM to return pass/fail judgment — this is subjective AI judgment, not a deterministic shell command.
findings.correction: AI checks should remain available but require explicit acknowledgment (e.g., a 'confidence: vibes-only' flag or a separate 'allow-ai-checks' project config). Alternatively, AI checks should always be paired with a deterministic fallback shell command.
findings.test_to_write: tests/ai-check-determinism.test.ts — test that running the same AI check twice on unchanged workspace returns consistent results, then confirm that this test is inherently flaky (proving the 'vibes' nature).

findings.gap: When a check has no 'cmd' field and is not type: 'ai', runCheck() returns { passed: true, gaps: [] } without any warning. A mistyped check name or empty definition silently succeeds.
findings.evidence: find-gaps.ts:596-598: `if (!check.cmd) { return { passed: true, gaps: [] }; }` — no-op checks pass without even a console warning that the check has no executable definition.
findings.correction: Emit a warning (or fail closed) when a check has neither cmd nor a recognized type. A check that does nothing should not silently pass.
findings.test_to_write: tests/empty-check-warning.test.ts — test that defining a check with no cmd and no type produces a warning-level gap rather than silently passing.
